title: "Eigenvector Computation and Low-Rank Approximations"
description: "Original mathematical teaching with a worked delivery-operations example; MML §10.4."
---

**Study reference:** Deisenroth, Faisal & Ong, *Mathematics for Machine Learning*, §10.4. The examples, reasoning and notation explanations are written independently.

## Start from a problem

A compact matrix approximation can be formed using the leading singular directions. PCA thus connects covariance eigenvectors with the truncated SVD of centered data.

## Formulate the problem mathematically

$$
X_c=U\Sigma V^\top,\quad (X_c)_k=U_k\Sigma_kV_k^\top,\quad S=\frac{V\Sigma^2V^\top}{N-1}
$$

This relation identifies the required structure. Interpret the symbols using the stated model rather than memorising the formula without its assumptions.

## Derive a worked result

For centered matrix diag(3,1), retaining only its first singular direction gives rank-one matrix diag(3,0), leaving squared Frobenius error 1. The first right singular vector is also the leading eigenvector of X_c^T X_c.

## Why the mathematics matters

Singular values quantify retained energy. Sign flips of principal vectors are arbitrary: v and -v represent the same one-dimensional subspace.

## Explain or calculate

If singular values are 5 and 2, how much squared energy is retained after keeping only the first component?
